chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam and others, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Prophet (may Allah's blessings be upon him and his family) delivered a sermon at Mina and said: 'O people! Whatever comes to you from me that accords with the Book of Allah, I said it; and whatever comes to you opposing the Book of Allah, I did not say it.'

key_terms.خَطَبَ بِمِنًى: Delivered a sermon at Mina — referring to the Prophet's address during the farewell pilgrimage
key_terms.كِتَابَ اللَّهِ: The Book of Allah (Quran) — used as the supreme criterion for authenticating hadith
key_terms.يُخَالِفُ: Opposes, contradicts — used for narrations that are inconsistent with the Quran
key_terms.يُوَافِقُ: Accords with, is in agreement with — used for narrations that conform to the Quran

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about hadiths that contradict the Quran?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) narrates that the Prophet (SAWW) delivered this famous sermon at Mina during his final pilgrimage, establishing the Quran as the ultimate criterion for validating hadith. This hadith, known in hadith sciences as one of the key 'ard al-hadith' (presentation of hadiths to the Quran) narrations, teaches that only those narrations conforming to the Quran are authentic. The original audience—pilgrims gathered at Mina—would have understood this as a foundational methodological principle for the community after the Prophet's passing.

en.hubeali:
Muhamad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazan, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hisham Bin Al Hakam and someone else, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘The prophet<sup>saww</sup> addressed at Mina, so he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘O you people! Whatever comes to you all from me<sup>saww</sup> which is in accordance with the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so I<sup>saww</sup> have said it, and whatever comes to you opposing the Book of Allah<sup>azwj</sup>, so I<sup>saww</sup> did not say it’’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn ’Isma‘il from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hisham ibn al-Hakam and others from abu ‘Abdallah (a.s.) who has said the following.

“The holy Prophet once addressed the people in Mina (a place in Makkah) saying, “O people, whatever comes to you in the form of my Hadith you must see if it agrees with the holy book of Allah then know that I have said it but whatever comes to you that does not agree with the book of Allah then know that I have not said it.”
